rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient covering nearly the full organic range at moderate temperature to reveal the elution window for all 6 compounds while reducing risk of truncation. The 20 min slope should give useful spacing information without making the first run excessively long.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the next step is to cut analysis time by trimming the gradient to the apparent elution window and making it steeper. The first peak corresponds to roughly 0.13 organic and the last to about 0.43, so 0.15–0.70 over 10 min should keep all compounds in-gradient while testing how much runtime can be reduced without sacrificing resolution.

Resolution is still far above the 1.5 threshold, so the best chance to improve CRF is to shorten the run slightly while keeping the same window and temperature. Dropping tG from 10 to 8 min directly tests how much time can be removed before the earliest pair begins to approach the limit.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so now the goal is to map the shortest robust fully resolved method. Since all pairs still have a large margin at tG 8, reducing to 6 min checks whether more speed is possible before any pair drops toward the 1.5 resolution limit.

Resolution remains comfortably above 1.5 even at 6 min, with the first pair still the limiting one, so another 2 min reduction is the most efficient way to locate the shortest acceptable method. Keeping phi0, phi1, and T fixed isolates the effect of gradient steepness.

The limiting pair is still well above the 1.5 cutoff at tG 4, so the next step is to test the minimum allowed gradient time. This will identify whether the absolute shortest gradient on this window still preserves full-resolution credit.

At tG 2 the only failure is the earliest pair, so lowering phi0 should retain and spread those first peaks while keeping the run very short. Keeping phi1 and T fixed isolates whether a slightly weaker starting composition can recover full resolution at the minimum gradient time.

Lowering phi0 hurt the first pair, so instead I would narrow the window from the top to make the 2 min gradient shallower while leaving early conditions unchanged. Dropping phi1 one step should increase spacing for the critical pair with minimal effect on overall runtime because the last peak is already very early.

The 2 min run nearly recovered full credit when phi1 was lowered to 0.65, so one more step to 0.60 is the cleanest test of whether a slightly shallower minimum-time gradient can push the first pair above R = 1.5. The last peak is still very early, so there is room to trade a bit more retention for resolution.

We already have a 1.000 method at the minimum gradient time, so the remaining question is whether temperature can shorten it further without losing the critical first-pair resolution. Raising T one step should reduce retention, especially for the late peak, while checking whether selectivity remains adequate on this optimized 2 min window.

Higher temperature hurt the limiting first pair, so the better way to refine the minimum-time method is to make the 2 min gradient slightly shallower again by lowering phi1 one more step. This should strengthen the early separation while still keeping the last peak comfortably before 10 min.
